rule.unknown.label: Unclassified: {path}
rule.unknown.effect: Disk Steward has no rule for these files, so it never offers them for cleanup. They are listed so the space they use stays visible.
rule.prot.credentials.label: Credentials and keys
rule.prot.credentials.effect: Sign-in tokens, private keys and certificates. Never offered for cleanup: removing one signs you out or locks you out of a service, and nothing rebuilds it.
rule.prot.databases.label: Databases
rule.prot.databases.effect: SQLite, LevelDB and similar database files. Removing one loses the history, settings or index inside it and can corrupt an app that has it open.
rule.prot.git.label: Git repositories
rule.prot.git.effect: A .git folder holds the full history of a project. Removing it deletes that history and nothing rebuilds it.
rule.codex.state-tmp.label: Codex state temp files
rule.codex.state-tmp.effect: Half-written copies left behind when Codex saved its global state. Codex works from the real state file and writes new temp files when it needs them.
rule.codex.runtime-install.label: Interrupted Codex runtime installs
rule.codex.runtime-install.effect: Leftover folder of a runtime download that never finished. Codex downloads the runtime again if it needs it.
rule.codex.runtimes.label: Codex runtimes
rule.codex.runtimes.effect: Language runtimes and tools Codex downloads to run code. Removing one makes Codex download it again, at about the same size, the next time it needs it.
rule.codex.logs.label: Codex logs
rule.codex.logs.effect: Log files of past Codex sessions. They only matter for troubleshooting; Codex writes new ones as you use it.
rule.codex.cache.label: Codex catalog caches
rule.codex.cache.effect: Plugin and model catalogs Codex downloaded. Codex fetches them again on its next start.
rule.codex.browser-cache.label: Codex browser caches
rule.codex.browser-cache.effect: Web caches of the Codex desktop app. Quit the app first; it refills them as you use it.
rule.codex.electron.cache.label: Codex desktop caches
rule.codex.electron.cache.effect: Chromium caches of the Codex desktop app: web cache, compiled code and GPU shader caches. Quit the app first; it recreates them on the next start, which can be slightly slower once.
rule.codex.component-cache.label: Codex component cache
rule.codex.component-cache.effect: Downloaded browser components of the Codex desktop app. Quit the app first; it downloads them again when needed.
rule.codex.sparkle.label: Codex update leftovers
rule.codex.sparkle.effect: Downloaded update files that stayed behind. The app downloads an update again if one is available.
rule.codex.sessions.label: Codex sessions ({path})
rule.codex.sessions.effect: Rollout files of past Codex conversations. Archiving keeps a compressed copy you can restore; deleting makes the conversation unrecoverable.
rule.codex.archived-sessions.label: Archived Codex sessions
rule.codex.archived-sessions.effect: Rollout files of conversations you archived in Codex. Archiving here keeps a compressed, restorable copy; deleting removes the conversation for good.
rule.codex.state.label: Codex settings and state
rule.codex.state.effect: Configuration, session index, history and sign-in state of Codex. Never offered for cleanup: removing a file resets that part of Codex or hides past sessions from its list.
rule.codex.plugin-staging.label: Codex plugin staging
rule.codex.plugin-staging.effect: Working files while Codex installs or updates plugins. Protected because Codex may be using them.
rule.codex.user-content.label: Codex user content ({path})
rule.codex.user-content.effect: Skills, rules, memories, automations, attachments and generated files you or Codex created. Never offered for cleanup because nothing rebuilds them.
rule.claude.logs.label: Claude logs
rule.claude.logs.effect: Debug and telemetry logs of Claude Code and Claude Desktop. They only matter for troubleshooting; new ones are written as you work.
rule.claude.electron.cache.label: Claude Desktop caches
rule.claude.electron.cache.effect: Chromium caches of Claude Desktop: web cache, compiled code and GPU shader caches. Quit the app first; it recreates them on the next start, which can be slightly slower once.
rule.claude.cli-cache.label: Claude Code web cache
rule.claude.cli-cache.effect: Cached web fetches and tool downloads of the claude command. It fetches them again when needed.
rule.claude.net-cache.label: Claude Desktop network cache
rule.claude.net-cache.effect: HTTP cache of Claude Desktop. Quit the app first; it refills as you use it. The Cache.db database files stay protected.
rule.claude.shipit.label: Claude Desktop update leftovers
rule.claude.shipit.effect: Downloaded update files that stayed behind. The app downloads an update again if one is available.
rule.claude.cli-versions.label: Old Claude Code versions
rule.claude.cli-versions.effect: Earlier installs of the claude command. The version your claude command points to and the newest one are kept. Removing an older one does not affect the command, and you can reinstall it at any time.
rule.claude.cli-versions-dir.label: Old Claude Code versions (folders)
rule.claude.cli-versions-dir.effect: Earlier installs of the claude command stored as folders. The version your claude command points to and the newest one are kept. Removing an older one does not affect the command.
rule.claude.desktop-engines.label: Old Claude Desktop engines
rule.claude.desktop-engines.effect: Claude Code engines bundled with older Claude Desktop releases. The newest one and the version pinned in .sdk-version are kept. Quit the app first; it downloads an engine again if it needs one.
rule.claude.projects.label: Claude Code sessions ({path})
rule.claude.projects.effect: Conversation transcripts, sub-agent runs and tool outputs of a project. Archiving keeps a compressed copy you can restore; deleting removes the ability to resume or search those conversations.
rule.claude.file-history.label: Claude Code file history
rule.claude.file-history.effect: Backups of files Claude Code edited, used to rewind changes. Archiving keeps a restorable copy; deleting means those edits can no longer be rewound.
rule.claude.vm-images.label: Claude Desktop VM images
rule.claude.vm-images.effect: Disk images of the Claude Desktop sandbox VM. Quit the app first. Archiving keeps a compressed copy; deleting makes the app download and set up the VM again, which takes a while.
rule.claude.plugin-cache.label: Claude Code plugin cache
rule.claude.plugin-cache.effect: Downloaded copies of plugin versions. Versions that Claude Code lists as installed are kept; the others are fetched again if you install them.
rule.claude.memory.label: Claude Code memory
rule.claude.memory.effect: Notes Claude saved about you and your projects. Never offered for cleanup: removing them makes Claude forget what it learned, and nothing rebuilds them.
rule.claude.config.label: Claude Code settings
rule.claude.config.effect: Settings, instructions, custom agents, commands, skills and hooks written by you or your plugins. Never offered for cleanup: removing them resets your Claude setup.
rule.claude.desktop-state.label: Claude Desktop local data
rule.claude.desktop-state.effect: Chat state and sign-in data kept in the app's browser storage. Never offered for cleanup: removing it logs you out and clears local drafts.
rule.cursor.electron.cache.label: Cursor caches
rule.cursor.electron.cache.effect: Chromium caches of Cursor: web cache, compiled code and GPU shader caches. Quit Cursor first; it recreates them on the next start, which can be slightly slower once.
rule.cursor.vsix.label: Cursor extension download cache
rule.cursor.vsix.effect: Cached extension packages. Quit Cursor first; it downloads them again when you install or update an extension.
rule.cursor.cached-data.label: Cursor old code caches
rule.cursor.cached-data.effect: Compiled-code caches of earlier Cursor builds. The newest folder is kept. Quit Cursor first; it rebuilds what it needs on the next start.
rule.cursor.logs.label: Cursor logs
rule.cursor.logs.effect: Log files of past Cursor sessions. They only matter for troubleshooting; new ones are written as you use it.
rule.cursor.extensions.label: Cursor obsolete extensions
rule.cursor.extensions.effect: Extension folders that Cursor marked obsolete after an update. They are no longer loaded, and Cursor would remove them itself on a restart. Quit Cursor first.
rule.antigravity.electron.cache.label: Antigravity caches
rule.antigravity.electron.cache.effect: Chromium caches of Antigravity: web cache, compiled code and GPU shader caches. Quit Antigravity first; it recreates them on the next start, which can be slightly slower once.
rule.antigravity.vsix.label: Antigravity extension download cache
rule.antigravity.vsix.effect: Cached extension packages. Quit Antigravity first; it downloads them again when you install or update an extension.
rule.antigravity.cached-data.label: Antigravity old code caches
rule.antigravity.cached-data.effect: Compiled-code caches of earlier Antigravity builds. The newest folder is kept. Quit Antigravity first; it rebuilds what it needs on the next start.
rule.antigravity.logs.label: Antigravity logs
rule.antigravity.logs.effect: Log files of past Antigravity sessions. They only matter for troubleshooting; new ones are written as you use it.
rule.antigravity.extensions.label: Antigravity obsolete extensions
rule.antigravity.extensions.effect: Extension folders that Antigravity marked obsolete after an update. They are no longer loaded, and Antigravity would remove them itself on a restart. Quit Antigravity first.
rule.windsurf.electron.cache.label: Windsurf caches
rule.windsurf.electron.cache.effect: Chromium caches of Windsurf: web cache, compiled code and GPU shader caches. Quit Windsurf first; it recreates them on the next start, which can be slightly slower once.
rule.windsurf.vsix.label: Windsurf extension download cache
rule.windsurf.vsix.effect: Cached extension packages. Quit Windsurf first; it downloads them again when you install or update an extension.
rule.windsurf.cached-data.label: Windsurf old code caches
rule.windsurf.cached-data.effect: Compiled-code caches of earlier Windsurf builds. The newest folder is kept. Quit Windsurf first; it rebuilds what it needs on the next start.
rule.windsurf.logs.label: Windsurf logs
rule.windsurf.logs.effect: Log files of past Windsurf sessions. They only matter for troubleshooting; new ones are written as you use it.
rule.windsurf.extensions.label: Windsurf obsolete extensions
rule.windsurf.extensions.effect: Extension folders that Windsurf marked obsolete after an update. They are no longer loaded, and Windsurf would remove them itself on a restart. Quit Windsurf first.
rule.cursor.shipit.label: Cursor update leftovers
rule.cursor.shipit.effect: Downloaded update files that stayed behind. Quit Cursor first; it downloads an update again if one is available.
rule.antigravity.shipit.label: Antigravity update leftovers
rule.antigravity.shipit.effect: Downloaded update files that stayed behind. Quit Antigravity first; it downloads an update again if one is available.
rule.ollama.models.label: Ollama models
rule.ollama.models.effect: Downloaded language models. Disk Steward only reports the size; remove models with the command shown. Each model is downloaded again when you pull it.
evidence.tainted: Protected: this folder contains something that must not be removed automatically (reason: {reason}).
evidence.current_version: Kept: {version} is the version the claude command runs ({current}) or the newest installed ({newest}).
evidence.not_current_version: Not the version in use ({current}) and not the newest ({newest}).
evidence.version_unverifiable: Kept because the version in use could not be verified ({reason}).
evidence.engine_newest: Kept: {version} is the newest installed engine.
evidence.engine_pinned: Kept: {version} is the engine version pinned in .sdk-version.
evidence.plugin_manifest_unreadable: Kept because installed_plugins.json could not be read ({reason}), so installed plugins cannot be told apart.
evidence.plugin_installed: Kept: Claude Code lists this plugin as installed.
evidence.plugin_not_in_manifest: Claude Code does not list this plugin version as installed.
evidence.codex_both_indexed: Both IDs are listed in session_index.jsonl; Codex shows either one.
evidence.newest_dir: Kept: {name} is the newest folder here.
evidence.extension_obsolete: {name} is listed in .obsolete, so the editor no longer loads it.
taint.unreadable: folders that could not be read
scan.error.skipped_privacy: Skipped: a private or macOS-protected folder. Disk Steward never opens these.
scan.error.permission_denied: Not readable: permission denied. Give Disk Steward Full Disk Access to include it.
scan.error.other_volume: Skipped: this folder is on another volume.
scan.error.undecodable_name: Skipped: the name is not valid UTF-8.
scan.error.root_symlink: Skipped: this location is a symbolic link, and Disk Steward never follows symlinks.
scan.error.not_a_directory: Skipped: expected a folder but found a file.
evidence.codex_legacy_copy: Legacy-ID copy: the same session also exists as {partner}.
evidence.codex_duplicate_kept: Kept: this is the new-ID file of a session whose legacy-ID copy is {partner}.
evidence.codex_duplicate_unresolved: Looks like a duplicate of {partner}, but the ids or the content differ, so it stays in its normal group.
group.codex.sessions:duplicates.label: Codex sessions — legacy-ID copies
group.codex.sessions:duplicates.effect: Each file is the legacy-ID copy of a session that also exists under its new ID. Both IDs are normally indexed, so the thread may still be listed after this copy is gone. Archiving keeps a restorable compressed copy; deleting removes only the legacy-ID file.
rule.claude.desktop-workspaces.label: Claude Desktop agent workspaces
rule.claude.desktop-workspaces.effect: Each session folder is a whole agent workspace: your outputs and uploads, installed packages, audit keys and the account state of the nested .claude. Never offered for cleanup; manage them inside Claude.
rule.codex.artifact-runtime.label: Codex artifact runtime
rule.codex.artifact-runtime.effect: Working state of the Codex artifact runtime: a live socket in store/ and the current runtime generation. Never offered for cleanup; removing it breaks artifacts that are open.
rule.codex.plugin-exclusions.label: Codex plugin settings
rule.codex.plugin-exclusions.effect: The list of bundled plugins you switched off. Never offered for cleanup; removing it turns those plugins back on.
rule.prot.git-tree.label: Git work trees
rule.prot.git-tree.effect: Every file of a project that has a .git folder or file next to it, whatever the file is called. Never offered for cleanup: it may be uncommitted work that nothing else holds.
evidence.appeared_during_scan: Kept: this appeared after the scan started, so it was not checked.
evidence.sqlite_header: Kept: the file starts like a SQLite database, whatever its name says.
evidence.header_unreadable: Kept: the first bytes of the file could not be checked ({reason}).
scan.error.dataless_skipped: Skipped: a cloud placeholder folder; opening it would download it.
rule.app.electron.cache.label: Electron app caches ({path})
rule.app.electron.cache.effect: Chromium caches of an Electron app: web cache, compiled code and GPU shader caches. Quit the app first; it recreates them on the next start, which can be slightly slower once.
rule.app.sparkle.label: Update leftovers, Sparkle ({path})
rule.app.sparkle.effect: Update files that the Sparkle updater downloaded and left behind. The app downloads an update again if one is available. Nothing younger than a day is offered.
rule.app.updater-cache.label: Update leftovers ({path})
rule.app.updater-cache.effect: Pending updates, update.zip and block maps that an app's auto-updater kept. The updater downloads an update again if one is available. Nothing younger than a day is offered.
rule.app.shipit.label: Update leftovers, ShipIt ({path})
rule.app.shipit.effect: Downloaded update files of Electron apps that use the ShipIt updater. The app downloads an update again if one is available. Nothing younger than a day is offered.
rule.app.chrome-cache.label: Google Chrome cache
rule.app.chrome-cache.effect: One profile's cache folders (Cache and Code Cache) in Google Chrome, each removed whole. Quit Chrome first; pages load slower until the cache fills again. A folder counts as one item, as old as its newest file, so a browser in daily use is offered only when the age filter is low.
rule.app.chrome-beta-cache.label: Google Chrome Beta cache
rule.app.chrome-beta-cache.effect: One profile's cache folders (Cache and Code Cache) in Google Chrome Beta, each removed whole. Quit Chrome Beta first; pages load slower until the cache fills again. A folder counts as one item, as old as its newest file, so a browser in daily use is offered only when the age filter is low.
rule.app.chrome-canary-cache.label: Google Chrome Canary cache
rule.app.chrome-canary-cache.effect: One profile's cache folders (Cache and Code Cache) in Google Chrome Canary, each removed whole. Quit Chrome Canary first; pages load slower until the cache fills again. A folder counts as one item, as old as its newest file, so a browser in daily use is offered only when the age filter is low.
rule.app.brave-cache.label: Brave cache
rule.app.brave-cache.effect: One profile's cache folders (Cache and Code Cache) in Brave, each removed whole. Quit Brave first; pages load slower until the cache fills again. A folder counts as one item, as old as its newest file, so a browser in daily use is offered only when the age filter is low.
rule.app.edge-cache.label: Microsoft Edge cache
rule.app.edge-cache.effect: One profile's cache folders (Cache and Code Cache) in Microsoft Edge, each removed whole. Quit Edge first; pages load slower until the cache fills again. A folder counts as one item, as old as its newest file, so a browser in daily use is offered only when the age filter is low.
rule.app.arc-cache.label: Arc cache
rule.app.arc-cache.effect: One profile's cache folders (Cache and Code Cache) in Arc, each removed whole. Quit Arc first; pages load slower until the cache fills again. A folder counts as one item, as old as its newest file, so a browser in daily use is offered only when the age filter is low.
rule.app.chromium-cache.label: Chromium cache
rule.app.chromium-cache.effect: One profile's cache folders (Cache and Code Cache) in Chromium, each removed whole. Quit Chromium first; pages load slower until the cache fills again. A folder counts as one item, as old as its newest file, so a browser in daily use is offered only when the age filter is low.
rule.app.vivaldi-cache.label: Vivaldi cache
rule.app.vivaldi-cache.effect: One profile's cache folders (Cache and Code Cache) in Vivaldi, each removed whole. Quit Vivaldi first; pages load slower until the cache fills again. A folder counts as one item, as old as its newest file, so a browser in daily use is offered only when the age filter is low.
rule.app.headless-chrome.label: Headless Chrome leftovers
rule.app.headless-chrome.effect: Scratch folders (scoped_dir*) that headless Chrome runs left behind, as used by browser-automation tools and AI agents. Each run makes new ones. Nothing younger than a day is offered, so a run that is still going keeps its folder.
rule.app.spotify-cache.label: Spotify cache
rule.app.spotify-cache.effect: Spotify's cache folder. It may hold songs you downloaded for offline play, and you would have to download them again. Quit Spotify first.
rule.app.caches.label: App caches ({path})
rule.app.caches.effect: Cache folders apps keep in ~/Library/Caches. Apps rebuild them as needed, so the next use can be slower once. Cache.db databases and the files beside them stay protected. Nothing younger than a day is offered.
rule.app.logs.label: App logs and crash reports ({path})
rule.app.logs.effect: Log files and crash or diagnostic reports of apps. They only matter for troubleshooting; apps write new ones. Nothing younger than a day is offered.
rule.app.leftovers.label: Data of apps that are no longer installed
rule.app.leftovers.effect: Application Support folders named after an app that is not installed any more. Check before you remove one: it may hold documents or settings you want back if you reinstall the app. Only folders untouched for 90 days are offered, and moving to Trash is the default.
rule.app.tmp.label: Temporary files
rule.app.tmp.effect: Files that apps left in your temporary folder. Nothing younger than 3 days is offered, so files an app is still using stay.
rule.app.tmp-dir.label: Temporary folders
rule.app.tmp-dir.effect: Folders that apps left in your temporary folder. Nothing younger than 3 days is offered, so folders an app is still using stay. A folder with databases or credentials in it stays protected.
rule.app.user-cache-dir.label: Per-user system cache folders
rule.app.user-cache-dir.effect: Folders that apps keep in the per-user cache location of macOS. Apps rebuild them as needed. Nothing younger than 3 days is offered, and a folder with databases or credentials in it stays protected.
rule.vscode.electron.cache.label: VS Code caches
rule.vscode.electron.cache.effect: Chromium caches of VS Code: web cache, compiled code and GPU shader caches. Quit VS Code first; it recreates them on the next start, which can be slightly slower once.
rule.vscode.vsix.label: VS Code extension download cache
rule.vscode.vsix.effect: Cached extension packages. Quit VS Code first; it downloads them again when you install or update an extension.
rule.vscode.cached-data.label: VS Code old code caches
rule.vscode.cached-data.effect: Compiled-code caches of earlier VS Code builds. The newest folder is kept. Quit VS Code first; it rebuilds what it needs on the next start.
rule.vscode.logs.label: VS Code logs
rule.vscode.logs.effect: Log files of past VS Code sessions. They only matter for troubleshooting; new ones are written as you use it.
rule.vscode.extensions.label: VS Code obsolete extensions
rule.vscode.extensions.effect: Extension folders that VS Code marked obsolete after an update. They are no longer loaded, and VS Code would remove them itself on a restart. Quit VS Code first.
rule.user.packages.label: Libraries, archives and apps kept in your folders
rule.user.packages.effect: Photos, Music, Final Cut, Logic and similar libraries, Xcode archives, and apps outside Downloads. Each looks like a folder but is one document or one app. Never offered for cleanup; manage them in their own app.
rule.user.download-apps.label: Apps in Downloads ({path})
rule.user.download-apps.effect: Applications you downloaded and never moved to Applications. Make sure you do not run one from here, because it is gone once removed. Moving to Trash is the default.
rule.user.installers.label: Installers in Downloads ({path})
rule.user.installers.effect: Disk images and installer packages (.dmg, .pkg, .mpkg, .iso, .xip). Once the software is installed they are not needed, and you can download them again. Moving to Trash is the default.
rule.user.project-deps.label: Project dependencies ({path})
rule.user.project-deps.effect: node_modules, virtualenv and Cargo target folders next to a project. They are offered only when nothing in the project has changed for the idle period; the folders of an active project stay protected. npm install, pip install or cargo build recreates them.
rule.user.large.label: Large files ({path})
rule.user.large.effect: Files above the size limit. Only you know whether you still need them, so they are listed by size and last use. Moving to Trash is the default.
rule.user.idle.label: Idle files ({path})
rule.user.idle.effect: Big files you have not opened or changed for a long time. Deleting is permanent; moving to Trash, the default, is not.
rule.user.other.label: Other files in {path}
rule.user.other.effect: Everything in your folders that no rule offers. Listed so the space they use stays visible, and never offered for cleanup.
rule.dev.homebrew.label: Homebrew downloads
rule.dev.homebrew.effect: Bottles and source archives Homebrew downloaded. Disk Steward only reports the size; run the command shown. Homebrew downloads a package again when you reinstall it.
rule.dev.uv.label: uv cache
rule.dev.uv.effect: Wheels and source archives that uv shares between projects. Disk Steward only reports the size; run the command shown. uv downloads or builds them again when a project needs them.
rule.dev.pip.label: pip cache
rule.dev.pip.effect: Wheels and source archives pip downloaded. Disk Steward only reports the size; run the command shown. pip downloads them again on the next install.
rule.dev.npm.label: npm package cache
rule.dev.npm.effect: Packages npm downloaded. Disk Steward only reports the size; run the command shown. npm downloads them again on the next install.
rule.dev.npx.label: npx cache
rule.dev.npx.effect: Packages npx downloaded to run commands. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you. npx downloads a package again when you run it.
rule.dev.pnpm.label: pnpm store
rule.dev.pnpm.effect: The package store pnpm shares between projects. Disk Steward only reports the size; the command shown removes only packages no project links to.
rule.dev.yarn.label: Yarn cache
rule.dev.yarn.effect: Packages Yarn downloaded. Disk Steward only reports the size; run the command shown. Yarn downloads them again on the next install.
rule.dev.go-mod.label: Go module cache
rule.dev.go-mod.effect: Downloaded Go modules and their sources. Disk Steward only reports the size; run the command shown. Go downloads modules again on the next build.
rule.dev.go-build.label: Go build cache
rule.dev.go-build.effect: Compiled packages that Go reuses between builds. Disk Steward only reports the size; run the command shown. The next build is slower once.
rule.dev.cargo.label: Cargo registry
rule.dev.cargo.effect: Crate archives and sources Cargo downloaded. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you. Cargo downloads crates again when a build needs them.
rule.dev.gradle.label: Gradle caches
rule.dev.gradle.effect: Downloaded dependencies and build caches of Gradle. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you. Gradle downloads or rebuilds them on the next build.
rule.dev.maven.label: Maven local repository
rule.dev.maven.effect: Artifacts Maven downloaded, and artifacts you put there with mvn install. The ones you built yourself cannot be downloaded again. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you.
rule.dev.playwright.label: Playwright browsers
rule.dev.playwright.effect: Browser builds Playwright downloaded. Disk Steward only reports the size; run the command shown. Playwright downloads them again when a test run needs them.
rule.dev.puppeteer.label: Puppeteer browsers
rule.dev.puppeteer.effect: Browser builds Puppeteer downloaded. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you. Puppeteer downloads them again when a script needs them.
rule.dev.node-gyp.label: node-gyp headers
rule.dev.node-gyp.effect: Node.js headers node-gyp downloads to compile native add-ons. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you. node-gyp downloads them again when needed.
rule.dev.puccinialin.label: puccinialin Rust toolchain
rule.dev.puccinialin.effect: Rust toolchain files that Python build tools download on demand to compile Rust extensions. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you. They are downloaded again when a build needs them.
rule.dev.coresimulator.label: iOS Simulator devices
rule.dev.coresimulator.effect: Data of every simulated device, including the apps installed on it. Disk Steward only reports the size; the command shown removes only devices of Xcode versions that are gone. Other devices lose their apps and test data if removed.
rule.dev.xcode-derived-data.label: Xcode DerivedData
rule.dev.xcode-derived-data.effect: Build products and indexes of your Xcode projects. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you. Xcode rebuilds them, and the next build is slower. Quit Xcode before removing them.
rule.dev.xcode-device-support.label: Xcode iOS DeviceSupport
rule.dev.xcode-device-support.effect: Debug symbols Xcode copied from the iPhones and iPads you connected. Disk Steward can move a listed folder to the Trash for you. Xcode copies them again the next time you connect that device version.
rule.dev.colima.label: Colima virtual machine
rule.dev.colima.effect: The Colima VM, including its disk image with your containers, images and volumes. Disk Steward only reports the size; the command shown removes caches only. Deleting the VM loses local containers and volumes.
evidence.project_idle: Nothing in the project has changed for {days} days.
evidence.project_active: Kept: something in the project changed {days} days ago.
evidence.project_unreadable: Kept: the project folder could not be read ({reason}).
rule.app.steward-data.label: Disk Steward's own data
rule.app.steward-data.effect: Disk Steward's database and archives. Restore or remove archives on the Archives page; the database is rebuilt by the next scan.
